diagnosis: Molecular attributes of adrenal cortical carcinoma and adenoma
legend: Mechanisms underlying the development of adrenal cortical carcinomas (depicted to the left, in red) include overexpression of IGF2 and mutations in the WNT and p53 signalling pathways. Cell cycle–related genes are often upregulated, and chromosomal aberrations (usually deletions) are plentiful. Adrenal cortical carcinomas are furthermore characterized by global hypomethylation but increased promoter-specific hypermethylation, as opposed to adrenal cortical adenoma (right, in blue). In turn, adrenal cortical adenomas often lack WNT and p53 pathway mutations but instead exhibit mutations in genes encoding various ion channels (KCNJ5, ATP1A1, ATP2B3, CACNA1D, and CACNA1H) and in genes regulating PKA-related pathways (PRKACA and PRKAR1A). The transcriptome is overrepresented in genes associated with steroidogenesis, and chromosomal aberrations are few.

diagnosis: WNT and p53 pathways in adrenal cortical carcinoma
legend: Schematic representation of the WNT and p53 pathways in resting states and in adrenal cortical carcinoma. In its idle state, the WNT pathway main effector β-catenin is sent for ubiquitin-mediated proteolysis by a trimolecular complex (APC, GSK3β, and AXIN), and the p53 protein is regulated negatively in a similar manner by MDM2 (left). Adrenal cortical carcinomas recurrently demonstrate activating CTNNB1 (β-catenin) mutations (green star), which allows β-catenin to escape degradation and instead transport to the nucleus, where it will initiate transcription of WNT target genes, in turn promoting proliferation. This can also be achieved by inactivating mutations or deletions of the negative WNT regulators ZNRF3 and APC (pink stars). Upon cellular stress (e.g. extensive DNA damage), MDM2-mediated inhibition of p53 is lifted, leading to the activation of p53, which will promote DNA repair and apoptosis. However, in adrenal cortical carcinoma with inactivating TP53 gene mutations (pink star), this process is inhibited, leading to inhibited proliferation and accumulation of additional DNA damage.

diagnosis: Generalized multiomics profiles of adrenal cortical carcinoma (ACC)
legend: Via the pangenomic characterization of the mutational, chromosomal, expressional, and epigenetic landscapes of ACC, three main clusters have emerged, called cluster of clusters I–III (CoC I–III). CoC I ACCs exhibit the best prognosis of the three and are regularly associated with lower TNM stages. These tumours are characterized by a low frequency of mutations in WNT and p53 signalling pathway genes and associate to the mRNA expressional cluster C1B enriched for genes regulating immune response mechanisms. Furthermore, CoC I ACCs exhibit low levels of gene-specific methylation and are therefore characterized as CpG island methylator phenotype – low. Amplifications and whole-chromosome deletions are commonly seen, but whole-genome doubling (WGD) is rare. CoC II ACCs are considered an intermediate group of tumours in terms of prognosis and genetic aberrancies. CoC III ACCs exhibit the worst prognosis and the most advanced genetic imbalances; they are characterized by frequent mutations in WNT and p53 pathway gene members, expression of genes primarily associated to mitotic regulation (cluster C1A), and a high CpG island methylator phenotype. Chromosomal aberrations are frequent and scattered across the genome (noisy), and WGD is evident in the majority of CoC III ACCs.

legend: The cut surface of the tumour shows a yellowish-tan variegated appearance with necrosis and haemorrhage. The tumour shows no direct invasion into the kidney.
An example with diffuse solid and broad trabecular growth with tumour necrosis.
A conventional adrenal cortical carcinoma enriched in compact tumour cells with diffuse growth, variable cytological atypia, and an atypical mitotic figure.
Myxoid adrenal cortical carcinoma with abundant extracellular mucin deposition. The tumour cells show multiple mitotic figures.

Oncocytic adrenal cortical neoplasms are often assessed using the Lin–Weiss–Bisceglia system. This is an oncocytic adrenal cortical carcinoma that shows increased mitotic activity and coagulative tumour necrosis.
An oncocytic adrenal cortical carcinoma with focal comedonecrosis.
These can be biphasic with typical differentiated areas (shown here), or they can have a monophasic appearance that can simulate a sarcoma.
These can have a monophasic appearance (shown here) that can simulate a sarcoma, or they can be biphasic with typical differentiated areas.
Foci of venous angioinvasion (vascular invasion) in adrenal cortical carcinoma are characterized by intravascular tumour cells admixed with fibrin/thrombus.
In adrenal cortical carcinomas, atypical mitotic figures (arrow) are important findings suggestive of abnormal chromosome content.
Phosphohistone H3 immunohistochemistry can facilitate mitotic count in adrenal cortical carcinomas with low-grade features. Mitotic figures are marked on this photomicrograph.
An example with intratumoural proliferative heterogeneity demonstrated using Ki-67 immunohistochemistry. Most adrenal cortical carcinomas show a Ki-67 labelling index > 5%.
A pathologist-driven automated image analysis nuclear algorithm for the assessment of Ki-67 labelling index in an adrenal cortical carcinoma is illustrated.

diagnosis: Reticulin histochemistry in adrenal cortical tumours
legend: Adrenal cortical adenomas show a preserved nested reticulin framework (Gordon–Sweet silver).

diagnosis: Reticulin histochemistry in adrenal cortical tumours
legend: Unlike adrenal cortical adenomas, adrenal cortical carcinomas show a loss of reticulin framework (Gordon–Sweet silver).

SF1 is the most reliable biomarker for confirming the cortical origin. Diffuse nuclear SF1 expression is seen here in an adrenal cortical carcinoma. Note the absence of nuclear reactivity at sites of necrosis.
IGF2 paranuclear immunoreactivity has been shown as the most reliable translational biomarker in the distinction of adrenal cortical carcinoma from adenomas.
p53 overexpression can feature a subset of adrenal cortical carcinomas enriched in adverse molecular clusters.

Biologically aggressive adrenal cortical carcinomas tend to show nuclear β-catenin and/or aberrant p53 reactivity. Cytoplasmic and nuclear β-catenin expression is demonstrated here in an adrenal cortical carcinoma.

diagnosis: Mismatch repair immunodeficiency in adrenal cortical carcinoma
legend: MSH6 immunodeficiency in an adrenal cortical carcinoma is demonstrated. Mismatch repair immunohistochemistry is considered to screen for the possibility of Lynch syndrome–related pathogenesis. In addition, the combination of mismatch repair and PDL1 immunohistochemistry also helps determine eligibility for immunotherapy in select patients.

title: Reticulin algorithm
tablehtml:
Criteria:

Altered reticulin framework in association with one of the following features indicates malignancy:

·   Mitotic count: > 5 mitoses/10 mm2 (50 HPF of 0.2 mm2)

·   Tumour necrosis

·   Vascular invasion

tablehtml:

Venous invasion

Large size (> 100 mm and/or > 200 g)

Necrosis

Capsular invasion

Sinusoidal invasion

Malignant: At least one major criterion

Uncertain malignant potential: At least one minor criterion

Benign: Absence of major and minor criteria
